recipes.name: Spanish potato omelette
recipes.method_note: Low and slow. A high heat burns the bottom before the middle sets.

steps.instruction: Peel {{ing:potato-medium}}. Slice thinly. Slice {{ing:onion-medium}} thinly.
Heat {{ing:olive-oil}} in a non-stick frying pan on a low heat.
Add potato and onion. Cook 20 minutes, turning now and then, until soft.
steps.note: They should go soft, not crisp.

steps.instruction: Beat {{ing:egg-medium}} with {{ing:salt}} in a large bowl.
Tip the potato into the eggs. Stir. Leave 5 minutes.
Pour back into the pan on a low heat. Cook 10 minutes, until the edges set.
Put a plate over the pan. Turn it over in one go.
steps.note: Use oven gloves. Or finish it under a hot grill instead.

steps.instruction: Slide back in. Cook 5 minutes, until set in the middle.

recipes.name: Chickpeas with spinach and cumin
recipes.method_note: The fried bread thickens the sauce. Gluten-free bread works too.

steps.instruction: Heat {{ing:olive-oil}} in a large pan on a medium heat.
Fry {{ing:bread-slice-medium}} for 3 minutes, until golden. Lift onto a plate.
Slice {{ing:garlic-clove}}. Fry 1 minute, until pale gold.
Stir in {{ing:cumin-ground}} and {{ing:paprika}}. Cook for 30 seconds.
Add {{ing:passata}} and {{ing:white-wine-vinegar}}.
Drain {{ing:chickpeas-tinned}}. Stir in with 150 ml water.
Tear the fried bread in. Simmer (small bubbles) 10 minutes, until thick.
Stir in {{ing:spinach}} until wilted, about 2 minutes.

recipes.name: Chorizo and butter bean stew
recipes.method_note: The chorizo colours the oil red. That oil is where the flavour is.

steps.instruction: Slice {{ing:chorizo}} into rounds. Chop {{ing:onion-medium}} and {{ing:pepper-bell}}.
Heat {{ing:olive-oil}} in a large pan on a medium heat.
Fry the chorizo for 3 minutes, until the oil runs red.
Add the onion and pepper. Fry 8 minutes, until soft.
Crush in {{ing:garlic-clove}}. Stir in {{ing:paprika}}.
Add {{ing:chopped-tomatoes-tinned}} and drained {{ing:butter-beans-tinned}}.
Simmer (small bubbles) for 15 minutes, until thick.
Chop {{ing:fresh-parsley}}. Scatter over to serve.

recipes.name: Crispy potatoes with spicy tomato sauce
recipes.method_note: Parboiling first gives a fluffy middle and a crisp outside.

steps.instruction: Heat the oven to 220C.
Cut {{ing:potato-large}} into bite-sized cubes. Boil for 5 minutes. Drain.
Toss on a tray with 2 tablespoons of the oil and {{ing:salt}}.
Roast for 35 minutes, until golden and crisp. Turn halfway.
Heat the rest of {{ing:olive-oil}} in a small pan. Crush in {{ing:garlic-clove}}.
Add {{ing:paprika}}, {{ing:chilli-powder}}, {{ing:passata}} and {{ing:sugar-caster}}.
Simmer (small bubbles) 10 minutes, until thick.
Spoon the sauce over the potatoes to serve.

recipes.name: Roast cauliflower with romesco sauce
recipes.method_note: Romesco is a roasted pepper and almond sauce. It keeps a week in the fridge and is good with fish, eggs or toast.

steps.instruction: Heat the oven to 220C.
Cut {{ing:cauliflower-head}} into thick slices and florets.
Drain {{ing:chickpeas-tinned}}. Toss with the cauliflower, 2 tablespoons of the oil and 1 teaspoon paprika.
Quarter {{ing:pepper-bell}}. Add to a second tray with {{ing:garlic-clove}}, unpeeled.
Roast both trays 25 minutes, until charred at the edges.
Toast {{ing:almonds}} and {{ing:bread-slice-medium}} in a dry pan, 3 minutes.
Squeeze the garlic from its skins into a blender.
Add peppers, almonds, bread, {{ing:white-wine-vinegar}}, {{ing:salt}} and the last paprika.
Blend with the rest of {{ing:olive-oil}} until thick and nearly smooth.
Spread romesco on plates. Pile the cauliflower on top. Scatter {{ing:fresh-parsley}}.

swaps.text: Sunflower seeds, for a nut-free romesco
